title: Many in Gen Z See Influencing as a Real Career
paragraphs: In the past, many children dreamed of becoming doctors, teachers or sports stars. Today, many young people dream of becoming influencers, people who earn money by sharing content on social media.

According to a survey by the research company Morning Consult, about 57% of Gen Z, people born between the late 1990s and early 2010s, want to become influencers. In addition, 53% of young people said they think being an influencer is a respectable career. About three in ten even said they would pay money to try to become an influencer.

Even younger children seem to have very similar dreams. A 2025 survey by Whop, a company that helps people sell things online, found that more than 30% of children aged 12 to 15 want to become influencers or YouTubers.

Now, at least one university is offering a degree for future influencers. Arizona State University in the US has created a new program in content creation. Students learn how to build a personal brand and make videos, podcasts and social media posts. Students can study online or at the university's campuses in Phoenix or Los Angeles.
However, studying this new subject is not cheap at all. For students from outside the state, the program at the Los Angeles campus costs about $25,000 a year.
Not all surveys agree, though. One poll in 2026 found that far fewer young people want to be influencers than in the past. So, it is not clear if this dream will stay popular.
